section_summary: This section comprises State Department correspondence, SCAP reports, and intelligence documents concerning Japanese base metal resources, metallurgical industries, and postwar allocations between March 1946 and February 1947. Key records include negotiations among U.S., British, and French authorities over pricing and export quotas for stockpiled Japanese antimony, copper, tin, and lead, alongside SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 61 detailing Japan's wartime tungsten and molybdenum metallurgy. Later materials investigate commercial bauxite potential in the Palau Islands and evaluate wartime mineral discoveries along the Burma-Siam Railroad through interrogations of repatriated Japanese officers.

subfiles.about: The British Embassy requests an allocation of Japanese antimony stocks to prevent a shutdown of UK smelting operations before Bolivian shipments arrive.
subfiles.from: F. C. Everson, British Embassy, Washington
subfiles.summary: Everson formally claims Japanese antimony stocks for the United Kingdom to avert smelting shutdowns prior to receiving Bolivian supplies.
subfiles.title: Letter from F. C. Everson to Roswell H. Whitman regarding Japanese Antimony Allocation
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, JK Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: The U.S. Commercial Company recommends minimum export prices for Japanese antimony, copper, tin, and lead to protect RFC procurement programs.
subfiles.from: Charles B. Henderson, Chairman of the Board, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Henderson recommends fair U.S. port prices for Japanese antimony, copper, tin, and lead to prevent disrupting Government buying programs.
subfiles.title: Letter from Charles B. Henderson to William L. Clayton regarding Japanese Metal Export Prices
subfiles.to: William L. Clayton, Assistant Secretary of State

subfiles.about: The State Department proposes higher export prices for Japanese copper, lead, and tin to maximize Japan's capacity to pay occupation costs.
subfiles.from: William L. Clayton, Assistant Secretary of State
subfiles.summary: Clayton proposes higher export prices for Japanese copper, lead, and tin to reflect world markets and help fund occupation costs.
subfiles.title: Letter from William L. Clayton to Charles B. Henderson regarding Export Prices for Japanese Metals
subfiles.to: Charles B. Henderson, Chairman of the Board, Reconstruction Finance Corporation

subfiles.about: The State Department notifies the British Embassy of a minor f.o.b. price adjustment for Japanese antimony based on freight and insurance rates.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman advises Smart that the f.o.b. price for Japanese antimony metal has been adjusted to 17.2 cents per pound.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to J. A. Smart regarding Japanese Antimony Price Adjustment
subfiles.to: J. A. Smart, Raw Materials Section, British Embassy

subfiles.about: Whitman instructs USCC on applying uniform Japanese antimony prices to French and British purchases and expediting export shipments.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman provides Trout the British antimony price letter and approves sales terms to expedite antimony shipments to France.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to William H. Trout regarding Antimony Sales to Britain and France
subfiles.to: William H. Trout, Chief, Commercial Transactions Division, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Whitman explains the rationale for the 18.5-cent Japanese antimony price and affirms that existing commitments to Britain and France prevent any price increases.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman details how the 18.5-cent Japanese antimony price was established and concludes diplomatic commitments prevent revising prices upward.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Arthur Z. Gardiner regarding Antimony Export Pricing
subfiles.to: Arthur Z. Gardiner, Vice-President, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Kennedy surveys world antimony prices and recommends an equitable price of 18.5 cents per pound delivered New York for Japanese stocks.
subfiles.from: Harold D. Kennedy, Chief, Division of International Resources, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Kennedy reviews international antimony prices and recommends pricing Japanese export stocks at 18.5 cents per pound delivered New York.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from Harold D. Kennedy to Roswell H. Whitman regarding Price for Japanese Antimony
subfiles.to: Roswell H. Whitman, JK Division, Department of State

subfiles.about: The U.S. Political Adviser transmits SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 61 on tungsten and molybdenum metallurgy in Japan.
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 61, 'Tungsten and Molybdenum Metallurgy of Japan.'
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 753 from U.S. Political Adviser for Japan Transmitting Report on Tungsten and Molybdenum Metallurgy
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: A comprehensive technical survey of Japan's tungsten and molybdenum metallurgy, refining processes, plant facilities, ore sources, and historical production from 1925 to 1945.
subfiles.from: John D. Bardill, Scientific Consultant, Mining and Geology Division, Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: This report surveys the history, ore sources, metallurgy, and production statistics of Japan's tungsten and molybdenum refining industries from 1925 through 1945. It examines chemical refining and hydrogen-reduction techniques used to manufacture pure powders for lamp filaments, radio tubes, and tungsten carbide tools, with detailed descriptions of major plants including Mitsubishi's Tokyo Metal Works and Tokyo Shibaura Electric. In addition, extensive statistical tables document domestic mine outputs, concentrate imports from Korea, Manchuria, and the Americas, ferroalloy smelting volumes, and individual refinery capacities.
subfiles.title: Natural Resources Section Report No. 61: Tungsten and Molybdenum Metallurgy of Japan
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Parker transmits internal memoranda concerning the status, quality, and commercial prospects of bauxite deposits on Babelthuap Island in the Palau group.
subfiles.from: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Parker encloses three internal memoranda regarding the reserves, commercial viability, and administrative conditions for exploiting Palau bauxite deposits.
subfiles.title: Letter from G. R. Parker to Paul H. Nitze regarding Palau Bauxite Deposits
subfiles.to: Paul H. Nitze, Acting Director, Office of International Trade Policy, Department of State

subfiles.about: Parker requests an evaluation from the Office of Metals Reserve on the grade, commercial adaptability, and competitiveness of Babelthuap bauxite.
subfiles.from: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Parker solicits Johnson's expert opinion regarding the quality, refining adaptability, and market competitiveness of Babelthuap bauxite ore.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from G. R. Parker to Jesse C. Johnson regarding Bauxite Deposits in Palau Islands
subfiles.to: Jesse C. Johnson, Deputy Director, Office of Metals Reserve

subfiles.about: Parker reports Navy Military Government stipulations for admitting private commercial enterprises to develop bauxite in the Palau Islands.
subfiles.from: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Parker outlines Navy conditions for private Palau bauxite mining, including State Department approval, strict labor regulation, and native royalties.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from G. R. Parker to Arthur Z. Gardiner regarding Navy Conditions for Bauxite Mining in Palau
subfiles.to: Arthur Z. Gardiner, Vice-President, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Parker summarizes geological data compiled by Josiah Bridge on Babelthuap bauxite reserves, ore assays, remaining Japanese equipment, and prewar production figures.
subfiles.from: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company
subfiles.summary: Parker details Josiah Bridge's survey of Babelthuap bauxite, including reserve estimates, chemical assays, salvaged equipment, and Japanese production statistics.
subfiles.title: Memorandum from G. R. Parker to Arthur Z. Gardiner regarding Bauxite Deposits and Prewar Production in Palau
subfiles.to: Arthur Z. Gardiner, Vice-President, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Nitze acknowledges Parker's report on Palau bauxite deposits and asks to be kept apprised of commercial exploitation plans.
subfiles.from: Paul H. Nitze, Acting Director, Office of International Trade Policy, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Nitze thanks Parker for information regarding bauxite deposits in the Mandated Islands and requests continuing updates on exploitation possibilities.
subfiles.title: Letter from Paul H. Nitze to G. R. Parker regarding Palau Bauxite Exploitation
subfiles.to: G. R. Parker, Chief, Pacific Ocean Division, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: Whitman inquires into financial statements indicating USCC may have sold Japanese antimony to RFC below the approved 18.5-cent price.
subfiles.from: Roswell H. Whitman, Associate Chief, Division of Japanese and Korean Economic Affairs, Department of State
subfiles.summary: Whitman asks Gardiner to verify whether USCC sold Japanese antimony to RFC below the agreed 18.5 cents per pound.
subfiles.title: Letter from Roswell H. Whitman to Arthur Z. Gardiner regarding Japanese Antimony Sales Proceeds
subfiles.to: Arthur Z. Gardiner, Vice-President, U.S. Commercial Company

subfiles.about: The U.S. Political Adviser transmits SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 62, 'Ferroalloy Metallurgy of Japan.'
subfiles.from: Office of the U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Transmits copies of SCAP Natural Resources Section Report No. 62, 'Ferroalloy Metallurgy of Japan.'
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 799 from U.S. Political Adviser for Japan Transmitting Report on Ferroalloy Metallurgy
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Bishop transmits interrogation reports, SCAP Natural Resources Section studies, and maps regarding tin and mineral deposits discovered during construction of the Burma-Siam Railroad.
subfiles.from: Max W. Bishop, for U.S. Political Adviser for Japan, Tokyo
subfiles.summary: Bishop transmits Japanese interrogation reports, a SCAP memorandum, and maps concerning mineral deposits along the Burma-Siam Railroad.
subfiles.title: Despatch No. 858 from Max W. Bishop regarding Mineral Deposits Along Burma-Siam Railroad
subfiles.to: Secretary of State

subfiles.about: Former Burma Area Army Commander Heitaro Kimura is interrogated regarding prewar tin, tungsten, and mica mines in Burma and wartime operations.
subfiles.from: Lt. Oyama and T/Sgt. H. Oshiro, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ AFPAC
subfiles.summary: Kimura discusses prewar tin, tungsten, and mica mines in Burma, noting wartime production ceased and no new deposits were found.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Heitaro Kimura regarding Burma Tin and Mineral Mines
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, United States Army Forces Pacific

subfiles.about: Former Thailand Area Army Commander Akito Nakamura is interrogated regarding mineral discoveries during Burma-Siam railway construction.
subfiles.from: Lt. Oyama and T/Sgt. H. Oshiro, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ AFPAC
subfiles.summary: Nakamura states he never heard of any mineral discoveries during railway construction in Siam, though observing tin mining in Malaya.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Akito Nakamura regarding Burma-Siam Railway and Minerals
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, United States Army Forces Pacific

subfiles.about: Former railway transportation officer Mamoru Ito provides hearsay information on tungsten and tin mines near the Thailand-Burma railroad.
subfiles.from: T/3 K. Yano, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ FEC
subfiles.summary: Ito details his military movements and reports rumors of a tungsten mine at Takanoan and a tin mine at Kuie.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Mamoru Ito regarding Minerals Along Burma-Siam Railroad
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Far East Command

subfiles.about: Former civil engineer Noboru Imata recounts military railway service across Indochina, Malaya, Burma, and Siam, reporting no knowledge of Siamese mineral deposits.
subfiles.from: Pfc. Teruo Yamamoto, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ FEC
subfiles.summary: Imata recounts railway engineering service across Southeast Asia, noting tin in Malaya but having no knowledge of mineral deposits in Siam.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Noboru Imata regarding Southeast Asia Railway Construction and Minerals
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Far East Command

subfiles.about: Former railway engineer Yukichi Matsuda provides hearsay locations of a tin mine in Siam and a coal mine in Burma near the railroad.
subfiles.from: T/4 Isami Makio, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ FEC
subfiles.summary: Matsuda reports rumored locations of a tin mine southwest of Phurankashi and a coal mine northeast of Thanbyuzayat.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Yukichi Matsuda regarding Tin and Coal Mines in Siam and Burma
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Far East Command

subfiles.about: Former transportation officer Isamu Sugiyama describes the Burma-Siam Railroad route and reports hearsay information on tungsten, tin, and oil in the region.
subfiles.from: T/3 K. Yano, Central Interrogation Center, Allied Translator and Interpreter Section, GHQ FEC
subfiles.summary: Sugiyama describes the engineering specifications of the Thailand-Burma Railroad and reports tungsten at Takanonan, Yenangyaung oil, and Malayan tin.
subfiles.title: Interrogation Report on Isamu Sugiyama regarding Railway Route and Mineral Locations in Southeast Asia
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Far East Command

subfiles.about: A list and map reference of tin, tungsten, antimony, and lead-zinc mines in Burma and Siam known to have operated before or during World War II.
subfiles.from: Robert Y. Grant (signed by John B. Gregg), Mining and Geology Division, Natural Resources Section, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Lists prewar and wartime tin, tungsten, antimony, and lead-zinc mines in Burma and Siam, noting activity in Pilok and Sisawat.
subfiles.title: Memorandum for Record: Mines in Burma and Siam
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers

subfiles.about: Allied intelligence extract evaluating prewar and wartime dredging operations, equipment, power installations, and production capacities of tin mines in the Ranong district of Siam.
subfiles.from: Headquarters Air Command, South East Asia
subfiles.summary: Examines tin dredging operations of Ranong Consolidated and Bangrin Tin Dredging companies, detailing power plants, equipment, transport, and wartime activity.
subfiles.title: Intelligence Report Extract: Siamese Tin Mines
subfiles.to: Allied Intelligence / Military Intelligence Section, GHQ AFPAC

subfiles.about: A sketch map showing the Burma-Siam border, Burma-Siam Railway, and numbered locations of tin, tungsten, antimony, and lead mines.
subfiles.from: Natural Resources Section / Allied Intelligence, GHQ SCAP
subfiles.summary: Map showing the Burma-Siam border, railway route, and locations of tin-tungsten, antimony, and lead mines in Burma and Siam.
subfiles.title: Map: Location of Mines in the Burma-Siam Area
subfiles.to: General Headquarters, Supreme Commander for the Allied Powers
